title: Azure Functions and Serverless Computing
description: Discover serverless computing with Azure Functions, including triggers, bindings, and a simple C# function example.

data.text: **Serverless computing** means you write code without worrying about servers. Azure Functions runs your code only when it is triggered, and you pay only for the time it runs. If no one calls your function, you are not charged.

A function is a small, single-purpose piece of code. It starts when an event happens — called a **trigger** — and can read or write data using **bindings**. This lets you connect to queues, databases, HTTP endpoints, and timers without writing extra connection code.

data.title: Common Triggers
items: **HTTP trigger**: Runs when a URL is called.
**Timer trigger**: Runs on a schedule, like every 5 minutes.
**Queue trigger**: Runs when a message arrives in Azure Storage.
**Blob trigger**: Runs when a file is uploaded to storage.

data.title: HTTP-triggered Azure Function (C#)
data.content: This function returns a greeting when you call it with a name parameter.

data.text: The `[Function]` attribute gives your function a name. The `[HttpTrigger]` attribute tells Azure to start the function when an HTTP request arrives. The `AuthorizationLevel` setting controls who can call the endpoint.

terms.definition: The event that starts a function, such as an HTTP request or a timer.
A declarative connection to another service, like a database or queue.
A pricing model where you pay only for the time your functions run.

data.title: Important
data.text: Functions are great for event-driven tasks, but they are not designed for long-running processes. If your workload needs to run for hours, consider Azure Batch or container jobs instead.

data.title: Exercise: Identify Trigger Types
data.description: Match each scenario to the best Azure Functions trigger.
steps: Send a welcome email 10 minutes after a user signs up.
Resize an image every time it is uploaded to a storage container.
Aggregate sales data every night at 2 AM.
data.expectedOutcome: You can choose between timer, blob, and queue triggers based on event type.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service.
Triggers start functions; bindings connect them to other services.
You pay only for execution time, not idle servers.
Functions work best for short, event-driven tasks.
data.takeaway: Serverless with Functions lets you ship features fast without managing infrastructure.
